lead: A `..` below a component that does not exist is collapsed on Windows and refused everywhere else; no case may assert either.
body: `Core\IO::within($base, "nothing/..")` answers `$base` on Windows and throws `IOError` on Linux, because `nvs_config::capability::resolved` asks the platform canonicalizer first and Win32 normalizes `nothing\..` out before the syscall while `realpath` stops at the missing component. Use a `..` whose parent exists (`io-within-resolves-and-then-proves-containment.nvst` does) or a name that merely contains `..`.
